editorial_contributions.text:
The authors investigate the concept of topological Markov fields (TMF) in one dimension that is a new property of a shift space. Some relations beetwen a TMF and other notions such as Markov chain, topological Markov chain (TMC), Markov random field (MRF) and sofic shift are established. One of the main results is as follows:

 Let \(X\) be a shift space. Then the following statements are equivalent:

 (1) \(X\) is the support of a stationary Markov chain

 (2) \(X\) is the support of a stationary MRF

(3) \(X\) is non-wandering and a TMF

(4) \(X\) is a TMC consisting of a finite union of irreducible TMCs with disjoint alphabets.

 As a consequence, the authors deduce that stationary MRF is a Markov chain.

Another main result is a finite procedure for checking whether a given sofic shift is a TMF where the input data is a labeled finite directed graph-presentation of a shift.

title.title: Mixing properties of colourings of the \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) lattice

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Fix \(d\geq 2\). Given a finite undirected graph \({\mathcal{H}}\) without self-loops and multiple edges, consider the corresponding `vertex' shift, \(\text{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{d},{\mathcal{H}})\), denoted by \(X_{{\mathcal{H}}}\). In this paper, we focus on \({\mathcal{H}}\) which is `four-cycle free'. There are two main results of this paper. Firstly, that \(X_{{\mathcal{H}}}\) has the pivot property, meaning that, for all distinct configurations \(x,y\in X_{{\mathcal{H}}}\), which differ only at a finite number of sites, there is a sequence of configurations \(x=x^{1},x^{2},\ldots,x^{n}=y\in X_{{\mathcal{H}}}\) for which the successive configurations \(x^{i},x^{i+1}\) differ exactly at a single site. Secondly, if \({\mathcal{H}}\) is connected ,then \(X_{{\mathcal{H}}}\) is entropy minimal, meaning that every shift space strictly contained in \(X_{{\mathcal{H}}}\) has strictly smaller entropy. The proofs of these seemingly disparate statements are related by the use of the `lifts' of the configurations in \(X_{{\mathcal{H}}}\) to the universal cover of \({\mathcal{H}}\) and the introduction of `height functions' in this context.

title.title: Four-cycle free graphs, height functions, the pivot property and entropy minimality

editorial_contributions.text:
A Borel \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) dynamical system \((X,S)\) is almost Borel universal if any free Borel \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) dynamical system \((Y,T)\) whose Gurevich entropy is strictly smaller than the topological entropy of \((X,S)\) is isomorphic to a Borel subsystem \((X,S)\), after removing a null set. The authors study a sufficient condition for a topological \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) dynamical system \((X,S)\) to be almost Borel universal by introducing flexible marker sequences \((C_n)_{n=1}^{\infty} \in (2^X)^{\mathbb{N}}\), where \(C_n\) is a finite subset of \(X\). They show that if a topological \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) dynamical system \((X,S)\) admits a flexible marker sequence \((C_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}\), then any free Borel \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) dynamical system having entropy less than \[h(C):=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\frac{1}{\vert \{-n, \dots, n\}^d\vert}\log \vert C_n\vert\] almost Borel embeds in \((X,S)\). In the case where \(h(C)=\infty\), any free Borel \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) dynamical system almost Borel embeds in \((X,S)\). 

The authors prove that a generic homeomorphism of a compact manifold of topological dimension at least 2 can model any ergodic transformation. They also show that nonuniform specification implies almost Borel universality, which was originally obtained by \textit{D. Burguet} [Ergodic Theory Dyn. Syst. 40, No. 8, 2098--2115 (2020; Zbl 1447.37018)], and that proper \(k\)-colorings of \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) for all \(k\geq 3\) and for all \(d\geq 1\), and domino tilings of \(\mathbb{Z}^2\) are almost Borel universal.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: In 2000, Cohn, Kenyon and Propp studied uniformly random perfect matchings of large induced subgraphs of $\mathbb Z^2$ (a.k.a. dimer configurations or domino tilings) and developed a large deviation theory for the associated height functions. We establish similar results for large induced subgraphs of $\mathbb Z^3$. To formulate these results, recall that a perfect matching on a bipartite graph induces a flow that sends one unit of current from each even vertex to its odd partner. One can then subtract a ''reference flow'' to obtain a divergence-free flow. We show that the flow induced by a uniformly random dimer configuration converges in law (when boundary conditions on a bounded $R \subset \mathbb R^3$ are controlled and the mesh size tends to zero) to the deterministic divergence-free flow $g$ on $R$ that maximizes $$\int_{R} \text{ent}(g(x)) \,dx$$ given the boundary data, where $\text{ent}(s)$ is the maximal specific entropy obtained by an ergodic Gibbs measure with mean current $s$. The function $\text{ent}$ is not known explicitly, but we prove that it is continuous and {\em strictly concave} on the octahedron $\mathcal O$ of possible mean currents (except on the edges of $\mathcal O$) which implies (under reasonable boundary conditions) that the maximizer is uniquely determined. We further establish two versions of a large deviation principle, using the integral above to quantify how exponentially unlikely the discrete random flows are to approximate other deterministic flows. The planar dimer model is mathematically rich and well-studied, but many of the most powerful tools do not seem readily adaptable to higher dimensions. Our analysis begins with a smaller set of tools, which include Hall's matching theorem, the ergodic theorem, non-intersecting-lattice-path formulations, and double-dimer cycle swaps.
